{"concepts_used":["GC-0115","GC-0046","GC-0102"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMM/Part61/3/3/1","quote":"a document: whose production the Registrar has required under paragraph 202(c) of the Act; and that the Registrar is satisfied should not be made available for public inspection"},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/3/3/1","quote":"a document that would be privileged from production in legal proceedings on the ground of legal professional privilege"},{"ref":"TMM/Part61/3/3/1","quote":"a document that is subject to an order of a court or tribunal that prohibits disclosure of the document or information in the document"}],"answer":"**Yes, the supplied Manual indicates that the Registrar can require production of documents—but these extracts do not establish the full legal power or its limits.**

**Manual practice:** Part 61 expressly refers to documents whose production the Registrar has required under paragraph 202(c) of the Act. It also refers to the Registrar being satisfied that those documents should not be available for public inspection. Requiring production and allowing public inspection are therefore distinct matters in that passage. [TMM/Part61/3/3/1]

**When does that go too far?** The supplied passages do not answer the legal limits of a production requirement. Section 202(c) itself is not included in the supplied Act extracts, so I cannot establish from them which documents may be demanded, from whom, or on what grounds a demand may be challenged.

**Potential protections mentioned in the Manual:** Part 61 lists documents protected by legal professional privilege and documents subject to a court or tribunal order prohibiting disclosure. However, those references do not themselves establish whether either protection excuses compliance with a Registrar’s production requirement. Nor does protection from public inspection necessarily answer whether a document must be produced. [TMM/Part61/3/3/1]

The cautious examiner-facing conclusion is: the Manual recognises a production power attributed to s 202(c), but the actual provision and any applicable legal limits are needed before assessing whether a demand exceeds that power."}
